tip: In the perfect tense an adverb like redan sits between har and the participle: har redan ätit, not har ätit redan.
When the owner is clear from context, Swedish uses the definite instead of a possessive: har förlorat passet, not sitt pass.
berätta needs för before the listener: berättade för mig means told me. You cannot drop the för.
The -s on ses makes it reciprocal: vi ses means we see each other, the everyday way to say see you.
For a length of time Swedish uses i: bott i två år means lived for two years, not för.
klaga takes över for what you complain about: klagade över att means complained that. The preposition is fixed.
